### 2026-10-08 – Today, I started working on Starbie for the first time! (I wanted to get started earlier in the week, but I barely had any time). Today, I completed all the steps up to creating the ESP32 C3, as descr

**1.5h**

Today, I started working on Starbie for the first time! (I wanted to get started earlier in the week, but I barely had any time). Today, I completed all the steps up to creating the ESP32 C3, as described in the image.

A big reason I spent so much time on so few steps is that getting started (setting things up, I mean) took me a lot of time.

Even when trying to download KiCad, I was faced with immediate problems, which took me almost 20 minutes to navigate to AND to clear my treasured, high-storage downloads.

I tried to download the Week 1 Care Package, but it kept taking me to a GitHub Dev site... (the red code high-key terrified me)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pwNbc3CZtwBCGJ0ZksWAw7XQQPlAMTId/28c3ac05bbefa97ef56e055a16d815c6c0708af7234fef8cf82b5ff1524cc5d6.png)

Then, I tried to unzip the Week 1 Care Package.zip file, but my Mac wouldn't even let me do that!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pwNbc3CZtwBCGJ0ZksWAw7XQQPlAMTId/9fb246f9d2fb642da3708a447f8b37e6af20977c8f15d947cf6d49660da39443.png)

I had to research on Reddit, YouTube, and Google on how to open the .zip file without downloading an external app. I eventually ended up just redownloading it. Then, I began working on the actual components in the Schematic Editor. By this point, my brain was fried, and my computer was overloaded. I put the ESP32 C2 together with ease... then I moved on to the next step, adding the buttons, but the left-hand-side tiny green wire wasn't connecting to the label.
After further frustrating research, I realized... I wasn't even in the Schematic Editor canvas where I'm supposed to build my circuits in the first place!!! I was in the Symbol Editor layout! (according to a highly confident Google Gemini, which I was using to help me troubleshoot my various problems — see below.)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pwNbc3CZtwBCGJ0ZksWAw7XQQPlAMTId/f09501d5ab43725721f7b7052e17ccc00a4254f5a2478d93bac7838388bb23a3.png)

All in all? Objectively, I might "not have done a lot" with my 90 minutes of work time today. However, to me, my work is a massive win! I explored KiCad for the first time, learned about .sym and .pretty files for the first time (I found the ending .pretty to be super cute!), and worked in the Schematic Editor, which is a more advanced editing platform than I've ever seen before!

### 2026-10-09 – Today, I finished all five of the components up! I also moved my design from the Schematic Editor to the PCB Editor!

**3h**

Today, I finished all five of the components up! I also moved my design from the Schematic Editor to the PCB Editor!
Evidence:

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 at 7.52.53 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pwNbc3CZtwBCGJ0ZksWAw7XQQPlAMTId/8103f70db86808dfb3a72f579e7f4eb7f2ae3528a61c30e612d923aa42abba55.jpg)

Today's work session was really fun; I learned a lot about Schematic Editor, PCB Editor, how the two editors connect, and about assigning footprints!

I was able to put all of my components together much faster!! I got the hang of where to find parts and what each part meant. Learning about what each part means and how they all come together was really interesting!

Even though I ran into a few minor problems on the way, some quick research and troubleshooting with AI, as well as my own newfound, increasing understanding of Schematic Editor, helped me solve them quickly. One example was when I was confused about why my SW_Push button wasn't wiring to my label:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pwNbc3CZtwBCGJ0ZksWAw7XQQPlAMTId/e52d9ff429d3b26624af3627fb22d7f571845b4436719467760880e11233fdaf.png)

Reflecting on my feelings when creating the components, I felt a lot more confidence as I was able to put them together, especially the last two components (MPU6050 and the Environment Sensor)!

However, later on, I ran into a big problem. I had to spend almost 30 minutes figuring out why there were 4 errors when I was trying to move the design from the Schematic Editor to the PCB Editor... turned out that I accidentally assigned a footprint J2 with 1x04 pins instead of matching it with the 1x08!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pwNbc3CZtwBCGJ0ZksWAw7XQQPlAMTId/899c7131c2511a80a94cdd40db190364e345cb63cbe19691c21cb61cbc045e09.png)

 I fixed that and got to the mixed-up PCB page, which is where I left off for tonight. I have a busy day tomorrow, but I plan on spending at least a couple hours of my day arranging the components into a star shape, adding the star outline, checking for errors, and CUSTOMIZING!!!

Side note: To me, the background of the PCB Editor kind of looks like outer space!! :D
